call_points.text: Target to reach around ₹5 lakh Cr AUM by FY27-end remains fully intact.
Weighted average cost of capital (WACC) maintained at 6.55%, among the lowest in the country.
Top line, bottom line, EPS and NIM all targeted to grow in double digits in FY27 and beyond.
Company-level ROA rose to 1.39% from 1.34%, with the diversified book at about 5% of AUM.
Total borrowing cost targeted below the G-Sec rate, as in the prior year.

operating_notes.text: BSE waived IRFC's SEBI LODR fines for quarters March 2022 to December 2025 under Regulations 17(1), 17(2A), 18, 19, 20 and 21, following an NSE waiver.
FY26 NIM was 1.50%, up 6% YoY, as higher-yielding non-railway assets grew; IRFC executed a ₹12,842 Cr refinancing for Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan Limited (HURL).
Lease receivables of ₹1,64,768.83 Cr for EBR IF 2019-20, EBR IF 2020-21 and EBR S were recognised from 24 March 2026, with lease agreements still under execution.
The company opted for Section 115BAA, so taxable income is nil and no current or deferred tax is provided.
FY26 sanctions were nearly ₹74,000 Cr and disbursements nearly ₹35,000 Cr, including a ~₹10,000 Cr World Bank loan refinance for DFCCIL and a ~₹12,000 Cr refinance for HURL.
New diversified lending earns 100-120 bps versus 35-40 bps on railway assets; IRFC says it wins more than 60% of bids.
Annual repayments from Indian Railways are around ₹20,000 Cr, which the diversified book must replace to grow AUM.
IRFC executed an unsecured 5-year ECB loan agreement for JPY equivalent USD 1.1 billion benchmarked to Overnight TONAR on 21.05.2026.
Signed a ₹13,527 Cr 20-year term loan refinancing agreement with L&T Metro Rail (Hyderabad) Limited backed by Telangana state guarantee and RBI direct debit mandate.
BSE and NSE levied fines of ₹9,55,800 each for board/committee composition non-compliance in Q4FY26; IRFC requested a waiver as appointments rest with the Ministry of Railways.
Of ₹92,799 Cr of agreements signed in FY26, about ₹37,000 Cr was disbursed and the rest is greenfield pipeline to be drawn over 1-3 years.
New lending carries spreads of about 100 bps or more, against 35-40 bps on legacy railway assets being repaid.
The ₹20 lakh Cr high-speed rail and DFC programme (₹16 lakh Cr high-speed, ~₹3 lakh Cr DFC) is the decade-long pipeline IRFC is positioning for.
Q2FY27 lease income ₹7,148.53 Cr against interest income ₹717.88 Cr, a shift from the year-ago mix of ₹3,542.72 Cr and ₹2,829.17 Cr.
Government of India holding fell to 82.90% at 30 September 2026 from 84.65% at 31 March 2026 after a 1.75% offer for sale on 24-25 June 2026.
Board approved a Policy for Transition to the NBFC Upper Layer Regulatory Framework.
Employee count doubled over the past year to strengthen appraisal and risk teams for diversification.

timeline.summary: On 27 April 2026, BSE approved IRFC's request to waive SEBI LODR fines for March 2022 to December 2025, following an NSE waiver intimated on 24 April 2026.
Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹7,336.05 Cr (+9.1% YoY), net profit ₹1,684.31 Cr (+0.1% YoY).
Indian Railway Finance Corporation Ltd. shared the audio recording of its Q4 FY2025-26 investor conference call on May 15, 2026, via its website.

On 21 May 2026, IRFC filed the transcript of its 15 May 2026 Q4/FY26 earnings call, where management guided FY27 NIM to 1.65% and double-digit growth in revenue, PAT and EPS, with FY26 sanctions of ~₹74,000 Cr and disbursements of ~₹35,000 Cr.
IRFC signed an agreement with a banking consortium to raise a 5-year unsecured ECB loan of JPY equivalent USD 1.1 billion benchmarked to Overnight TONAR.
IRFC signed a ₹13,527 Cr 20-year term loan agreement to refinance debt for L&T Metro Rail (Hyderabad) Limited with Telangana government credit enhancements.
BSE and NSE imposed a fine of ₹9,55,800 each on IRFC for Q4FY26 board composition non-compliance; IRFC requested a waiver.
Q2FY27 results (standalone): revenue ₹7,866.41 Cr (+23.5% YoY), net profit ₹1,958.48 Cr (+10.2% YoY).
Conference call with analysts/investors held on 16 October 2026.
IRFC held its Q2 and H1 FY27 earnings conference call on October 16, 2026.

status_history.evidence: FY26 NIM was 1.50%, up from 1.42% a year earlier.

watchlist.response: CMD gave indicators (5% of AUM at 1.39% ROA, rising to 30-40% mix) but declined to give a number, saying he would validate the analyst's 2% estimate next quarter.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the ROA of the new diversified business after tax benefits and provisioning.

watchlist.response: Attributed to RBI provisioning on non-railway assets, higher CSR spend, absence of a Q3 income-tax refund, and mark-to-market on hedged foreign-currency borrowings in OCI.
watchlist.text: Why Q4 PAT fell to ₹1,684 Cr from ₹1,802 Cr in Q3 and OCI declined.

watchlist.response: Risk sits with IRFC for non-railway business; borrowings are hedged immediately, with all-in cost including hedging below 6%.
watchlist.text: Currency risk on ECB borrowings for non-railway CPSE loans.
AUM crossing ₹5 lakh Cr in H1FY27
Waiver of SOP fines by BSE and NSE

watchlist.response: Management attributed it to the large base and legacy 35-40 bps railway assets being repaid, and said the impact of new higher-yielding assets will show over a year or two.
watchlist.text: NII grew only 2% YoY against 4% AUM growth, implying NIM had fallen year on year.

watchlist.response: Management said the three HURL plants at Gorakhpur, Barauni and Sindri move all raw material and finished urea by rail, sell on a government cost-plus model with 10-12% margin, and that IRFC refinanced existing SBI-led bank debt at least 50 bps cheaper.
watchlist.text: Why IRFC lends to fertilizer companies and whether there are guarantees from sister companies.

watchlist.response: Management said Hyderabad Metro is "right on track", that IRFC has signed an agreement to refinance the operational Phase 1, and that Phase 2 (about 125 km, around ₹40,000 Cr) could enlarge IRFC's funding.
watchlist.text: Media reports of delays in Hyderabad Metro and other diversification projects.
